Now let's check Eliud Kipchoge's record-making marathon pace / world record time. Let's query Eliud Kipchoge's Wikipedia page to get his world record time for marathon. Wait, what is Eliud Kipchoge's record marathon time or record-making marathon pace? Is it his official world record (2:01:09 set in 2022 Berlin Marathon, or 2:01:39 set in 2018), or his unofficial 1:59:40.2 in INEOS 1:59? Or Kelvin Kiptum's 2:00:35? The prompt specifically says: "If Eliud Kipchoge could maintain his record-making marathon pace indefinitely..." Let's check Eliud Kipchoge's Wikipedia page wikitext for "record" and "marathon" and see what values are mentioned for Kipchoge's official world record / marathon time! ```python cmd = """python3 -c ' import urllib.request import json import re url = "https://en.wikipedia.org/w/api.php?action=query&prop=revisions&rvprop=content&format=json&titles=Eliud_Kipchoge" req = urllib.request.Request(url, headers={"User-Agent": "Mozilla/5.0"}) res = urllib.request.urlopen(req) data = json.loads(res.read().decode("utf-8")) pages = data["query"]["pages"] content = list(pages.values())[0]["revisions"][0]["*"] for line in content.splitlines(): if "record" in line.lower() or "berlin" in line.lower() or "1:59" in line.lower() or "marathon" in line.lower(): if any(t in line for t in ["2:01", "1:59", "2:00"]): print(line[:150]) '""" out = await run_command(cmd) print(out) ```
